title: App Signing, Upload Keys, CI, and Recovery Check

questions.prompt: Which design best applies app signing, upload keys, ci, and recovery?
options: Separate delivered app-signing identity from upload authentication and protect the whole audited release path.
Commit the keystore encrypted beside its password
Use the upload fingerprint for delivered-app restrictions
questions.answer: Separate delivered app-signing identity from upload authentication and protect the whole audited release path.
questions.explanation: The strongest option enforces authority at the correct boundary and includes limitations, lifecycle, adversarial verification, and recovery.

questions.prompt: Resetting a compromised upload key changes the signing certificate on APKs already delivered by Play.
questions.explanation: Using the irreplaceable app-signing key directly on every developer laptop increases exposure when a separate resettable upload key could be used.

questions.prompt: Why separate the upload key from the app-signing key?
questions.answer: The upload key can authenticate releases with less exposure and can be reset without changing the delivered app-signing identity.
questions.explanation: The answer identifies the specific security property and boundary required by the lesson rather than naming a library.
